verses.pali_roman: Puttā pi tassa bahavo indanāmā mahabbalā,
verses.english: His sons too are many, all named Inda, of great strength,

verses.pali_roman: Iddhimanto jutimanto vaṇṇavanto yasassino.
verses.english: possessed of power, of radiance, of beauty and of renown,

verses.pali_roman: Modamānā abhikkāmuṃ bhikkhūnaṃ samitiṃ vanaṃ.
verses.english: came rejoicing to the wood, to the assembly of bhikkhus.

verses.pali_roman: Uttarañca disaṃ rājā kuvero tap pasāsati.
verses.english: And the king who rules the northern quarter is Kuvera.

verses.pali_roman: Yakkhānaṃ ādhipati mahārājā yasassi so.
verses.english: Lord of the yakkhas, a great king of renown.

verses.pali_roman: Puttā pi tassa bahavo indanāmā mahabbalā,
verses.english: His sons too are many, all named Inda, of great strength,

verses.pali_roman: Iddhimanto jutimanto vaṇṇavanto yasassino.
verses.english: possessed of power, of radiance, of beauty and of renown,

verses.pali_roman: Modamānā abhikkāmuṃ bhikkhūnaṃ samitiṃ vanaṃ.
verses.english: came rejoicing to the wood, to the assembly of bhikkhus.

verses.pali_roman: Purimadisaṃ dhataraṭṭho, dakkhiṇena viruḷhako,
verses.english: Dhataraṭṭha in the eastern quarter, Viruḷhaka in the south,

verses.pali_roman: Pacchimena virūpakkho, kuvero uttaraṃ disaṃ.
verses.english: Virūpakkha in the west, Kuvera in the northern quarter.

verses.pali_roman: Cattāro te mahārājā samantā caturo disā
verses.english: Those four Great Kings, filling the four quarters all around,

verses.pali_roman: Daddallamānā aṭṭhaṃsu vane kāpilavatthave.
verses.english: stood blazing in the Kapilavatthu wood.

verses.pali_roman: Tesaṃ māyāvino dāsā āgū vañcanikā saṭhā
verses.english: Their servants came, deceivers, tricksters and frauds:

verses.pali_roman: Māyā kuṭeṇḍu veṭeṇḍu viṭuca viṭuṭo saha
verses.english: Māyā, Kuṭeṇḍu, Veṭeṇḍu, Viṭu and Viṭuṭa together,

verses.pali_roman: Candano kāmaseṭṭho ca kinnughaṇḍu nighaṇḍu ca,
verses.english: Candana and Kāmaseṭṭha, Kinnughaṇḍu and Nighaṇḍu,

verses.pali_roman: Panādo opamañño ca devasūto ca mātali,
verses.english: Panāda and Opamañña, and Mātali the devas' charioteer,

verses.pali_roman: Cittaseno ca gandhabbo naḷo rājā janosabho
verses.english: Cittasena the gandhabba, king Naḷa, Janosabha,

verses.pali_roman: Āgū pañcasikho ceva timbarū suriyavaccasā.
verses.english: Pañcasikha came, and Timbarū with Suriyavaccasā.

verses.pali_roman: Ete caññe ca rājāno gandhabbā saha rājubhi
verses.english: These and other kings, gandhabbas together with their kings,

verses.pali_roman: Modamānā abhikkāmuṃ bhikkhūnaṃ samitiṃ vanaṃ.
verses.english: came rejoicing to the wood, to the assembly of bhikkhus.

verses.pali_roman: Athāgū nābhasā nāgā vesālā saha tacchakā.
verses.english: Then came the nāgas of Nābhasa, and those of Vesālī with the Tacchakas.

verses.pali_roman: Kambalassatarā āgū pāyāgā saha ñātibhi.
verses.english: The Kambalas and Assataras came, and those of Payāga with their kin.

verses.pali_roman: Yāmūnā dhataraṭṭhā ca āgū nāgā yasassino.
verses.english: The Yāmuna nāgas and the Dhataraṭṭhas came, nāgas of renown.

verses.pali_roman: Erāvaṇṇo mahānāgo sopāga samitiṃ vanaṃ.
verses.english: Erāvaṇṇa the great nāga, he too came to the wood, to the assembly.

vocabulary.meaning: the fourth Great King, guardian of the north and lord of the yakkhas. Also called Vessavana. His three fellows were named on page 320
blazing, shining brilliantly. Said of the four Great Kings standing in the wood
illusionist, deceiver, fraud — the three words the verse uses of the Great Kings' servants, then followed by their names
Mātali, charioteer to Sakka. Named here among the gandhabbas as devasūta, the devas' driver
Eravanna, the great naga — the same name as Sakka's elephant Eravana, and here counted among the nagas who came

checks.issue: 'tap' AGAIN, THE SECOND SHEET TO PRINT IT. The line reads 'kuvero tap pasasati' exactly as page 320 verse 81 reads 'virulho tap pasasati', where the sense needs tam. Two separate sheets printing the same odd spelling makes it the book's consistent reading rather than a compositor's slip. Recorded as printed on both, NOT corrected on either.

TWO COLUMNS throughout, gutter measured as a clean corridor at x 963-1045. That is the THIRD different measure in three sheets — 319 had a hard right-column edge at x 1080, 320 a corridor at x 972-1188 — which is the argument for profiling every sheet rather than carrying one measurement forward.

A LONG RUN OF PROPER NAMES, verses 100 to 105, and they are the hardest lines on the sheet to read: Kutendu, Vetendu, Vituca, Vituto, Kinnughandu, Nighandu, Opamanno, Timbaru, Suriyavaccasa. Every one was read at 5x and every retroflex dot checked individually. Names carry no context to correct them from, so they are the lines in this section most worth a second pair of eyes against the book.

THE BOOK NAMES THE SAME KING TWO WAYS WITHIN SIX LINES. Verse 96 has 'virulhako' where page 320 verse 81 has 'virulho', and both are the southern Great King. The page prints both forms and neither was made to agree with the other.

The one departure from standard spelling, 'tap' at verse 91, is recorded in a check rather than quietly fixed.
